specPoints.text: calculate the concentration of a solution in mol dm −3 and g dm −3 Titration calculations are not required at this stage.

primer.text: How much solute sits in how much solution? This note answers in both currencies - mass concentration in g dm-3 and molar concentration in mol dm-3 - converts cm3 to dm3, then stretches the ruler for trace amounts: parts per million for solutions and volume-based ppmv for atmospheric gases.

lessons.title: Two currencies of concentration
lessons.opening: Concentration states how much solute sits in how much solution, and it speaks two currencies: mass per volume (g dm^-3) and moles per volume (mol dm^-3). This lesson converts between them through n = m/M and drills the dm^3 and cm^3 unit conversions.
keyPoints: Mass concentration in g dm^-3 = mass of solute / volume of solution in dm^3.
Molar concentration in mol dm^-3 = moles of solute / volume of solution in dm^3.
The two currencies connect through moles: n = mass / molar mass.
500 cm^3 must be converted to 0.500 dm^3 before any concentration division.

low.restatement: Divide the amount (grams or moles) by the volume in dm^3 to get the concentration; multiply concentration by volume to go back.
low.analogy: It is a density for dissolved stuff: how tightly the solute is packed into every litre of solution.
low.examPointer: Concentration triangles survive exams: amount on top, volume underneath.

medium.restatement: Because 1 dm^3 = 1000 cm^3, a cm^3 volume divides by 1000 before entering the equation; molar concentration then reuses the mass-to-moles bridge n = m / M that all stoichiometry shares.
medium.analogy: The two concentration units are like mph and km/h for the same journey - different dials, one underlying speed, converted through the molar mass gearbox.
medium.examPointer: State units at every line: g dm^-3 vs mol dm^-3 is a one-mark discriminator examiners love.

check.stem: 6.34 g of NaCl are dissolved to a final volume of 0.250 dm^3. What is the mass concentration?

options.explanation: Dividing 6.34 by 0.250 gives 25.4 g dm^-3 (3 s.f.).
That multiplies instead of dividing.
That inverts the fraction.
The arithmetic is right but the units are wrong - no moles were computed.

check.stem: Which expression converts a mass concentration into a molar concentration?

options.explanation: g dm^-3 divided by g mol^-1 leaves mol dm^-3.
Multiplication would give g^2 mol^-1 dm^-3 - meaningless.
The 1000 factor converts cm^3 to dm^3, unrelated to mass-to-mole conversion.
The particle count plays no role in concentration units here.

check.stem: 26.7 g dm^-3 of sodium bromide is the mass concentration. What mass sits in 500 cm^3?

options.explanation: 26.7 x 0.500 = 13.4 g; the cm^3 were converted first.
That forgot the cm^3-to-dm^3 division.
That divides instead of multiplying.
That ignores the volume entirely.

check.stem: If 6.34 g of NaCl (Mr 58.5) end up in 250 cm^3 of solution, what molar concentration results?

options.explanation: n = 6.34/58.5 gives 0.1084 mol; dividing by the 0.250 dm^3 volume gives 0.434 mol dm^-3.
That is the mass concentration wearing wrong units.
That stops at moles without dividing by volume.
The volume was divided by 1000 twice.

check.stem: A 1.25 mol dm^-3 sodium carbonate solution is needed using 250 g of solute (Mr = 106.0). What volume results?

options.explanation: That is an order of magnitude short.
The moles were divided wrongly.
That misplaces the decimal by two places.

check.stem: State the equation for molar concentration.
check.modelAnswer: Molar concentration in mol dm^-3 = number of moles of solute / volume of solution in dm^3.

check.stem: State the conversion between cm^3 and dm^3 used in concentration work.
check.modelAnswer: 1 dm^3 = 1000 cm^3, so a volume in cm^3 is divided by 1000 to enter concentration equations in dm^3.

check.stem: Explain why mixing up g dm^-3 and mol dm^-3 produces answers that are wrong by the molar-mass factor.
check.modelAnswer: A mass concentration already contains grams per volume, while a molar concentration contains moles per volume; skipping the n = mass / molar mass step leaves the grams unconverted, so the numeric answer stays larger by exactly the molar mass in g mol^-1 while the units silently mismatch.

check.stem: 6.34 g of NaCl end up dissolved in 250 cm^3 of solution. Calculate the molar concentration, using Mr(NaCl) = 58.5, to 3 s.f.
check.modelAnswer: n = 6.34 / 58.5 gives 0.1084 mol; volume = 0.250 dm^3; c = 0.1084 mol over 0.250 dm^3 lands at 0.434 mol dm^-3.

lessons.title: Parts per million
lessons.opening: Trace amounts need a bigger ruler: parts per million. This lesson defines 1 ppm as 1 mg in 1 dm^3, applies it to pool dosing, and converts to the volume-based ppmv used for atmospheric gases.
keyPoints: 1 ppm means 1 mg of solute in 1 dm^3 of water, a 1-in-10^6 ratio.
Pool chlorine at 3 ppm in 2.5 million litres works out at 7.5 kg maximum.
For gases, ppmv compares volumes: 1 cm^3 of gas in 1 x 10^6 cm^3 of air.
ppm (gas) = volume of gas x 10^6 / volume of air, in matching units.

low.restatement: One ppm is one milligram dissolved in one cubic decimetre - a millionth by mass; for gases it is one cubic centimetre in a million.
low.analogy: One ppm is one second in eleven and a half days - too dilute to spot directly, too important to ignore.
low.examPointer: Quote the definition in mg dm^-3 terms; 'very small' alone earns nothing.

medium.restatement: Because 1 dm^3 of water weighs 1 kg, 1 mg per dm^3 is 10^-3 g in 10^3 g, exactly 1 in 10^6; the same ratio in volume units is the ppmv convention for air.
medium.analogy: The ppm scale is a zoom lens: it stretches tiny ratios onto numbers you can hold, the way a microscope magnifies slides.
medium.examPointer: The gas identity never enters the ppm arithmetic - only volumes do; examiners use that as a trick-check.

check.stem: What mass of solute defines 1 ppm in 1 dm^3 of water?

options.explanation: One milligram in one cubic decimetre is the working definition.
A gram would be a thousand times too concentrated.
That is a thousand times too dilute.
That is not a trace amount at all.

check.stem: A pool holds 2.5 million litres and chlorine should stay at or below 3 ppm. What maximum chlorine mass does that allow?

options.explanation: The mg-to-kg conversion was missed.
The mg-to-kg conversion overshot by 100x.
That is a factor of 100 low.

check.stem: Which expression combines a gas volume with an air volume to yield ppm?

options.text: (volume of gas x 10^6) / volume of air
options.explanation: Volumes in the same units scale the ratio up by a million.

options.text: volume of gas / volume of air
options.explanation: That gives a tiny fraction, not ppm.

options.text: (mass of gas x 10^6) / volume of air
options.explanation: Gas ppmv compares volumes, not masses.

options.text: volume of air x 10^6 / volume of gas
options.explanation: The fraction is inverted.

check.stem: 152 cm^3 of ozone in 112 dm^3 of air: why must both volumes enter the ppm equation in matching units?

options.text: The two volumes carry different units, so 152 cm^3 becomes 0.152 dm^3 before the ratio
options.explanation: ppm arithmetic requires matching units on top and bottom.

options.text: Ozone must be converted to oxygen first
options.explanation: The gas identity plays no role.

options.text: dm^3 values are never usable in ppm work
options.explanation: Any units work if both sides match.

options.text: The 10^6 factor already handles the conversion
options.explanation: The factor scales the ratio; it does not convert units.

check.stem: 2.5 dm^3 of carbon dioxide dispersed in 10000 dm^3 of air: what ppm do the volumes give?

options.explanation: A decimal slipped in the scaling.
The division by 10000 lost a zero.
That is the raw fraction, unscaled.

check.stem: Define 1 ppm in terms of mass and volume for aqueous solutions.
check.modelAnswer: 1 ppm corresponds to 1 milligram dissolved in one cubic decimetre of water - equivalently 1 mg per kilogram, since that volume of water weighs a kilogram.

check.stem: State what the v in ppmv denotes and the volume pair it compares.
check.modelAnswer: The v marks concentration by volume: 1 ppmv means 1 cm^3 of the gas in 1 x 10^6 cm^3 (1000 dm^3) of air.

check.stem: Explain why the identity of the gas is irrelevant when calculating an atmospheric concentration in ppm.
check.modelAnswer: The ppm formula uses only the volume of the gas and the volume of the air, so the ratio depends on how much space the gas occupies, not on what the molecules are; the same 2.5 dm^3 in 10000 dm^3 of air is 250 ppm whether the gas is carbon dioxide or sulfur dioxide.

check.stem: Calculate, in ppm, the gas concentration when 2.5 dm^3 of sulfur dioxide spreads through 4000 dm^3 of air, using the volume ratio.
check.modelAnswer: ppm = (2.5 x 10^6) / 4000 = 625 ppm - the gas identity never enters the arithmetic.

glossary.definition: The mass of solute per cubic decimetre of solution, quoted in g dm^-3.
The moles of solute per cubic decimetre of solution, quoted in mol dm^-3.
A trace-concentration unit: 1 mg per dm^3 of water, or by volume 1 cm^3 of gas per 10^6 cm^3 of air.

workedExample.prompt: What molar concentration results when 6.34 g of sodium chloride dissolves into 250 cm^3 of solution? (Mr of NaCl = 58.5)
steps: Convert the volume: 250 cm^3 makes 0.250 dm^3.
Moles of NaCl: dividing 6.34 by 58.5 leaves 0.1084 mol.
Molar concentration: 0.1084 mol spread over 0.250 dm^3 is 0.434 mol dm^-3.
